examples.title: An honest student
examples.blurb: Asks for sources, picks each with a reason, reads, says what they think in their own words, drafts, then writes the essay.
questions: Paragraph 3 says: "A 10 percent fall in rent removes about 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years.". This point doesn't appear earlier in your work in the Room. Where did it come from?

The sentence "Mrs Wong, who has lived in a unit for nine years, supports a hard cap and believes landlords will never leave because the units are their pension [D4p2]." cites D4p2. Does that passage say this? Please look at it again with us.
The sentence "The landlords' association argues the opposite, that a hard cap is confiscatory and members will exit [D5p2]." cites D5p2. Does that passage say this? Please look at it again with us.

The sentence "I think a smaller cut should cost less supply, since losses grow with the size of the rent cut [D6p1], but that is my own inference and not a finding." cites D6p1. Does that passage say this? Please look at it again with us.

examples.title: An honest student who barely talks
examples.blurb: Reads and writes a real essay but says almost nothing in the Room. Shows the limit: silent thinking leaves no trace, so a person is asked to hear it.

examples.title: Outside AI writes it, then narrates it into the Room

examples.title: Outside AI plus a revision loop
examples.blurb: Reads how the report works, checks the draft, sends the Coach's questions to an outside AI and rewrites. Took as much typing as an honest student.

examples.title: Keeps the essay, answers the questions afterwards
examples.blurb: Insists on the finished essay and gets an outside AI to answer every question. The answers come after the claims were written.
